candidates.source_name: Athanasius of Alexandria / Epistola ad Epictetum
candidates.source_attribution: Athanasius of Alexandria, Epistola ad Epictetum (Letter to Epictetus, Bishop of Corinth), in Select Writings and Letters of Athanasius, Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers (NPNF), Series 2, Vol. 4, ed. Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Epictetum (c. 350 AD)

'Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God' — Athanasius marks Iēsoun Christon en sarki elēlythota (Jesus Christ in-flesh having-come) as the FOUNDATIONAL ANTI-DOCETIC CREEDAL FORMULA. The en sarki (in-flesh) is non-negotiable: the genuine-fleshly-advent of the Word excludes Docetic phantasm-Christology and Apollinarian rationalist-Christology alike. The Letter to Epictetus addresses precisely this controversy in Athanasius's own era: certain Egyptian-Christians had argued that the Word's-flesh was homoousios with the Word's-divinity (a kind of Apollinarian-reductionism in reverse). Athanasius vigorously denies this: the Word's-flesh is genuine-Mary-derived-human-flesh, NOT a divine-derivative; the Word is-from-the-Father, the flesh is-from-the-Virgin.

Archibald Robertson (Oxford / T&T Clark, 1892). PD. Greek text in Migne PG 26 (1857).

Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.59 (c. 350 AD)

'In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him' — Athanasius marks ton Huion autou ton monogenē (his ONLY-BEGOTTEN Son) as the UNIQUE-GENERATION anchor: monogenēs names the Son as uniquely-from-the-Father's-essence (monos-genos = of-one-kind / of-the-same-kind-as-the-Father-alone), distinct from any creature's-coming-into-being. The Latin tradition translates as unigenitus (only-begotten); the Greek monogenēs is more-precisely 'unique-of-his-kind.' The uniqueness excludes creature-categorization (the Son is NOT first-among-many-creatures) and the begotten-genos excludes the Spirit-pneumatomachian reduction (the Son's-generation is from-Father-essence, not creaturely-act). Pairs with Jn 1:18 (monogenēs theos — the only-begotten-God) and Jn 3:16 as the canonical monogenēs Christological-trio.

candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Epistola ad Epictetum (c. 350 AD)

'Hereby know ye the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God' — Athanasius marks Iēsoun Christon en sarki elēlythota (Jesus Christ in-flesh having-come) as the FOUNDATIONAL ANTI-DOCETIC CREEDAL FORMULA. The en sarki (in-flesh) is non-negotiable: the genuine-fleshly-advent of the Word excludes Docetic phantasm-Christology and Apollinarian rationalist-Christology alike. The Letter to Epictetus addresses precisely this controversy in Athanasius's own era: certain Egyptian-Christians had argued that the Word's-flesh was homoousios with the Word's-divinity (a kind of Apollinarian-reductionism in reverse). Athanasius vigorously denies this: the Word's-flesh is genuine-Mary-derived-human-flesh, NOT a divine-derivative; the Word is-from-the-Father, the flesh is-from-the-Virgin.

candidates.draft_body:
Athanasius of Alexandria Orationes contra Arianos III.59 (c. 350 AD)

'In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him' — Athanasius marks ton Huion autou ton monogenē (his ONLY-BEGOTTEN Son) as the UNIQUE-GENERATION anchor: monogenēs names the Son as uniquely-from-the-Father's-essence (monos-genos = of-one-kind / of-the-same-kind-as-the-Father-alone), distinct from any creature's-coming-into-being. The Latin tradition translates as unigenitus (only-begotten); the Greek monogenēs is more-precisely 'unique-of-his-kind.' The uniqueness excludes creature-categorization (the Son is NOT first-among-many-creatures) and the begotten-genos excludes the Spirit-pneumatomachian reduction (the Son's-generation is from-Father-essence, not creaturely-act). Pairs with Jn 1:18 (monogenēs theos — the only-begotten-God) and Jn 3:16 as the canonical monogenēs Christological-trio.
